input: lists is an outer list of k heads, 0 <= k <= 4294967295. Each head is None or a finite, acyclic, nondecreasing singly linked list. All nodes across all lists are distinct: shared tails and repeated head references are excluded. There are at most 4294967295 total nodes. Caller-owned ListNode objects have ordinary writable val/next data fields; val is an integer in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], and next is a node or None. Integers are plain int, excluding bool; lists and strings are ordinary list/str values rather than subclasses. Standard built-ins are unmodified; no concurrent mutation or custom field access occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The first original node of one nondecreasing merge, or None when all lists are empty. Equal values are stable within each original list and ordered by original list index across lists. Every original node appears exactly once; no value-only copy replaces a node.
mutation_aliasing: The outer lists list and its head references remain unchanged, but original node next fields are rewired. Values and node identities remain intact. External aliases to original heads/nodes observe the final merged edges. The final list is acyclic and None-terminated. Private round-head arrays and helper sentinels are allocated; sentinels are never returned. No state persists between calls.
numeric: Values are compared without arithmetic. k, total node count, paired-array indices and round lengths are safe integers. Pair-loop index+1 and final index+=2 remain at most 4294967296, which is exact. Sentinel objects carry no numeric value that could collide with an input value.
complexity: O(k + N*log(k+1) + 1) time for N total nodes, including copying k heads and processing empty runs. O(k+1) live auxiliary head-array space plus one active sentinel; old and next round arrays are both charged. Across all rounds O(k+1) head slots and O(k+1) sentinel objects are allocated. Each node participates in at most ceil(log2(k)) stable pairwise merges. No recursion, heap or new output nodes are used.
